doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Buddy Rich, Alvino Rey and Manhattan School
title: Buddy Rich's band personnel and later stints
summary: Mandel names players in Buddy Rich's early band, says they hated each other at first but got along on later stints through 1948, then mentions Georgie Auld and Alvino Rey.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: So, let’s see, who are some of the other players on Buddy’s band that you can recall, there were the Swopes…

Well in the early band, there weren’t any really great soloist except for, let’s see, you know we had like, Bitsy Mullins was his trumpet player who was a very good swing style trumpet player of that time. But most of, . . . we had Louis Olds was a trumpet player there, there were a lot of all very good technical trumpet players. We had George Berg, was the tenor player, it was Aaron Sachs for a short time was his clarinet player. And then Tony Scott came in after him and you know Buddy Rich wasn’t terribly easy to work for in particularly in those days.

We hated each other in that first band. By the time I came back to the band, a year later, in ‘47 after I’d gone to Manhattan School of Music and all, the whole band had changed, he had gotten some real good guys in the band and the whole feeling was different. I was in two bands after that. And we got along great and the last Buddy Rich band I was in was in 1948, when I left to go to California and get my card ‘cause I always knew I’d live there. But that’s getting ahead of ourselves.

So, I was with that first Buddy Rich band, it wasn’t a thrilling musical experience, except watching Buddy play, I mean it was just phenomenal in itself; and after that I went with Georgie Auld. I played with Georgie Auld in a number of bands in the spring of ‘46, summer of ‘46, then I went with Alvino Rey after George Handy had been there.
